primitives.verbatim_quote: াভ# BREAKTHROUGH 2: gamecenter overview serves per-receiver separation, cushion, air yards `/api/gamecenter/overview?gameId=` returns `receivers.{home,visitor}[]` where each receiver carries `receptionInfo.{avgSeparation, avgCushion, avgAirYards}` — real tracking-derived contextual values — plus a **league baseline** `receivers.leagueAverageReceiverSeparation.avg = 2.9867`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\delta_{\\text{sep}}': 'dimensionless separation residual', '\\bar{s}_{\\text{rec}}': 'average receiver separation in yards', '\\bar{s}_{\\text{league}}': 'league average receiver separation in yards'}
primitives.assumptions: Separation data is derived from real-time tracking, baseline is stable across seasons, and residuals are normally distributed around the mean.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \bar{s}_{\text{rec}} \) approaches zero or exceeds physical limits of field geometry.

primitives.name: Tight End vs Wide Receiver Separation Differential
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Tight ends run far wider open than receivers**, a full yard beyond league average against receivers slightly below it.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Delta_{\\text{TE-WR}}': 'difference in average separation between tight end and wide receiver in yards', '\\bar{s}_{\\text{TE}}': 'average separation for tight ends in yards', '\\bar{s}_{\\text{WR}}': 'average separation for wide receivers in yards'}
primitives.assumptions: Data includes ≥3 targets per receiver, TE and WR roles are distinct and consistently labeled.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sample size for either group is insufficient or role ambiguity exists.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's role-based open-ness modeling; GSE uses it for coverage assignment logic.
layer2.telemetry: Separation differential between tight ends and wide receivers

primitives.name: Pre-Snap Cushion Independence from Post-Throw Separation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Cushion is pre-snap and separation post-throw, so their near-independence is expected physically — the finding is that pre-snap leverage carries almost no information about eventual separation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\rho(\\text{cushion}, \\text{separation})': 'Pearson correlation coefficient between pre-snap cushion and post-throw separation'}
primitives.assumptions: Cushion and separation are independent random variables under standard NFL coverage scenarios.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In high-pressure or blitz-heavy situations where pre-snap positioning may influence outcome.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSI for feature selection; in GSE for simplifying state-space models.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between pre-snap cushion and final separation

The core operator 'receiver separation residual' is defined as the deviation of observed separation from a fixed league average baseline (2.9867 yd), enabling normalized comparison across players and games. This residualization removes model bias and provides a vendor-anchored metric. The second primitive, 'tight end vs wide receiver separation differential', captures the strategic difference in spatial openness, where TEs operate 1 yard wider on average than WRs. The third primitive, 'pre-snap cushion independence,' reveals that pre-game positioning has minimal predictive value for final separation, confirming that spatial openness is a dynamic post-throw phenomenon. These primitives form a dual framework: one for comparative context (residuals), one for role-specific behavior (differential), and one for temporal causality (independence). Failure modes include small sample sizes, misclassification of player roles, and model drift over time. The epistemic structure supports both Bayesian inference (for probability of openness) and state-transition modeling (for situational awareness).
